knowledge_point.title: Finding the Derivative of an Expression With the Tangent Trigonometric Function

question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ Applying these formulas, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}+tan⁡x) \\  & =1\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})+1\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}})+1({sec}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{\sqrt{x}}+{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x>0 and cos(x)!=0 for radical templates; otherwise cos(x)!=0; evaluated points are regular
generation.sampling_policy: positive integer coefficients 1..6; fixed source evaluation point; explicit coefficient extension

We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x.$ Applying this formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\sqrt{x}+5tan⁡x) \\  & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{x}}+5{sec}^{2}⁡x \\  & =\frac{5+10\sqrt{x}{sec}^{2}⁡x}{2\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x>0 and cos(x)!=0 for radical templates; otherwise cos(x)!=0; evaluated points are regular
generation.sampling_policy: positive integer coefficients 1..6; fixed source evaluation point; explicit coefficient extension

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-tan⁡x) \\  & =-{sec}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\pi ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\pi ) & =-{sec}^{2}⁡\pi  \\  & =-1\cdot (-1)^{2} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the instantaneous rate of change is $-1.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(tan⁡x)={sec}^{2}⁡x$ and $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sin⁡x)=cos⁡x.$ Applying these formulas, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6tan⁡x+3sin⁡x) \\  & =6{sec}^{2}⁡x+3cos⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(0) & =6{sec}^{2}⁡(0)+3cos⁡(0) \\  & =6+3(1) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope is $9.$
